Docs.summary: Presents and dismisses modal pages for a single .

remarks.para: Register an in the application's service collection to supply an implementation. This is the extensibility point that lets an alternative platform backend render modal navigation without forking the framework: the framework keeps ownership of the cross-platform modal stack, page lifecycle events and the push/pop reconciliation loop, and only the visual presentation is delegated here.

The framework creates one instance per window and disposes it when the window is destroyed or when the window's handler changes. Implementations must therefore tolerate multiple create/dispose cycles and must not be shared between windows.
All members are invoked on the UI thread.

Dismissals that start on the platform. When the user dismisses a modal natively — an interactive swipe-to-dismiss, a hardware back press, a native close button — the framework does not observe it. The implementation must route it back through host.Window.Navigation.PopModalAsync() so the cross-platform modal stack and the page lifecycle events stay in sync. The framework then calls for that page as part of applying the pop, so must be idempotent and complete successfully when the native modal is already gone.

Disposal. is called when the window is destroyed and when the window's handler changes. The framework does not call for modals that are still presented at that point, so is solely responsible for dismissing and releasing every native modal the backend still owns. Do not assume , the window handler, or any platform view obtained through them is still usable there — teardown may already have disposed the window's service scope. Capture whatever cleanup needs while the instance is live and treat disposal as best effort. A disposed instance is never reused; a new one is created from the factory if the window gets a new handler. Exceptions thrown from are logged and do not interrupt window teardown or handler replacement.

remarks.para: While this returns the framework still records pushes and pops on the cross-platform modal stack and still raises the corresponding page lifecycle events, but it does not call or . When the backend becomes ready it must call so the queued operations are applied. Return unconditionally if the backend has no readiness requirement.

Deferring has an observable consequence for callers: Navigation.PushModalAsync and Navigation.PopModalAsync complete as soon as the framework has updated its own state, so they do not wait for the deferred presentation and cannot report a failure in it. See the remarks on for how deferred faults are reported.
Implementations may consult here. Do not try to derive this from the framework's overall modal readiness, which already folds this property in.

Docs.summary: Called when the window's page gets a handler, including when the page is replaced.

remarks.para: Use this to attach platform hooks that depend on the window's content being realized, such as a hardware back button handler. This may be called multiple times for the same window. It is also called once immediately after the instance is created when the window's page already has a handler, so a backend that resolves late does not miss the notification.

The framework guarantees it is never delivered twice for the same page-handler attachment, and that the built-in platform is never notified for an attachment that this instance handles. Notification is withheld until the window has a service scope — until then the framework cannot tell whether a factory is registered, and notifying the built-in platform early would leave its hooks installed alongside this instance's.
If this method throws, the framework logs the exception and continues attaching the page. The notification is considered delivered and is not retried for the same page-handler attachment.

Docs.returns: A task that completes once the modal is off screen.

remarks.para: Implementations are responsible for releasing the platform views created for . The framework detaches the page from its parent after this task completes.

This must be idempotent. It is called for a page the backend already dismissed natively when that dismissal is routed back through Navigation.PopModalAsync, and it must complete successfully rather than throw in that case.

If this task faults the framework puts back on , because a failed dismissal means the modal is presumed to still be on screen and dropping it would leave a visible modal that no stack knows about. The cross-platform modal stack is left without the page, so the next reconciliation pass retries the dismissal — and is preserved across that retry. As with , the fault is rethrown to the caller of Navigation.PopModalAsync only when the pop was applied inline; a deferred pop that faults is logged instead.

Docs.returns: A task that completes once the modal is on screen and safe to dismiss. The framework awaits this task before applying any further modal operation, so completing early can allow a subsequent pop to race the presentation.

remarks.para: If this task faults the framework removes from again, because the modal is not on screen. The cross-platform modal stack is left untouched, so Navigation.ModalStack still contains the page and the next reconciliation pass retries the presentation.

Where the fault surfaces depends on when the operation is applied. When was at request time the push is applied inline and the fault is rethrown to the caller of Navigation.PushModalAsync. When the push was deferred because was , that caller has already completed, so the fault is instead logged through the window's and cannot be observed by navigation code. Backends that need deferred failures to be actionable should surface them themselves.
